title: Update frontend to consume renamed balances.pairwise field
declaredInterface: No new interface - frontend now reads `balances.pairwise` instead of the removed `balances.settlements`, matching the backend's GET /balances response shape after the pairwise-balances change.
assumptions: Backend GET /balances was just changed (by me, this session) to return {net, pairwise} instead of {net, settlements}. The frontend (just pushed by a teammate) still references `settlements` in 3 files, which would silently break the Settle Up view. Fixing references only, not changing any UI/UX behavior.

completion.whatWasBuilt: Updated the frontend (App.jsx, BalancesView.jsx, StatsCards.jsx) to read balances.pairwise instead of the removed balances.settlements field, and refreshed related copy that described 'greedy debt minimization' / 'minimum transactions' since that's no longer what the backend computes.

decisions.decision: Kept internal variable/state names like `settlements` and the 'Settle Up' tab label in BalancesView.jsx
decisions.why: Only the API field name changed (settlements -> pairwise); the UI concept of a settle-up list is still valid, just backed by pairwise (not minimized) data now
decisions.alternativesConsidered: Renaming every internal identifier to 'pairwise' for consistency - rejected as unnecessary churn

filesChanged.purpose: Default/fallback balances state now uses pairwise: [] instead of settlements: []
Reads balances.pairwise for the stat count; renamed card title from 'Simplified Settle-ups' to 'Open Balances' to match new semantics
Reads balances.pairwise; updated descriptive copy that referenced debt minimization/minimum transactions

completion.knownLimitations: Verified with npm run build (succeeds) and a manual browser check of the empty-state UI; did not click through adding expenses in the browser end-to-end since backend logic was already unit-tested and curl-verified.
completion.nextSteps: None - frontend and backend are back in sync on the balances API shape.
